concepts.title: Mixtures: Types and Properties
concepts.definition: A mixture holds two or more substances that keep their own properties; homogeneous mixtures like salt solution look uniform throughout, while heterogeneous mixtures like sugar in sand show visible parts - and since no new substance forms, physical methods can undo the mixing.
concepts.key_idea: Mixed but unchanged: the parts of a mixture can always be separated physically.
concepts.textbook_ref: iesc105.txt sections on types and properties of mixtures
question_patterns: define a mixture and classify the given examples as homogeneous or heterogeneous
why can mixtures be separated by physical methods
differentiate a mixture from a compound
is air a homogeneous mixture - justify
list the properties that substances retain in a mixture
identify the type of mixture in the given situation

solution_steps.explain: Same composition throughout means homogeneous; visible parts mean heterogeneous.
No new substance forms and properties stay unchanged in a mixture.
Physical differences like size, solubility or boiling point drive the method.

concepts.title: Separation by Filtration, Evaporation and Decantation
concepts.definition: Insoluble solids leave liquids by filtration or by settling and decantation; dissolved solids return when the solvent evaporates - the path from sugarcane field to sugar crystals is exactly this craft at scale.
concepts.key_idea: Match the difference to the method: size filters, solubility evaporates.
concepts.textbook_ref: iesc105.txt sections on filtration, evaporation, decantation
question_patterns: how will you separate sand from water - name the method
how are sugar crystals obtained from sugarcane juice
when is decantation better than filtration
explain evaporation with a daily life example
which method separates the given mixture - justify
describe the steps of filtering a muddy water sample

solution_steps.explain: Insoluble solids filter out; dissolved solids need evaporation.
Filter paper, funnel or a dish for evaporation matches the mixture.
Residue and filtrate or crystals and vapour hold the separated parts.

concepts.title: Advanced Separation: Distillation, Chromatography and More
concepts.definition: Two miscible liquids separate by distillation when their boiling points differ; dyes in ink travel different distances on paper in chromatography; winnowing, threshing, magnetic separation and sublimation each exploit one physical difference of the mixture at hand.
concepts.key_idea: Every separation trick rides on one physical difference - boiling point, adhesion, magnetism or sublimation.
concepts.textbook_ref: iesc105.txt sections on distillation, chromatography and other methods
question_patterns: how will you separate two miscible liquids with different boiling points
explain chromatography with the example of ink
which method separates iron filings from sand - why
what is sublimation - give one example of separation by it
compare distillation and evaporation as separation methods
choose and justify a method to separate the given mixture

solution_steps.explain: Boiling point, solubility, magnetic nature or volatility of the components.
Distillation for boiling points, chromatography for adhesion, magnets for iron.
Check that each component is recovered without chemical change.
